(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; Times of Israel's own reporting language)

Hamas's interior ministry said the strike on an apartment building in the coastal Shati camp in the city killed Muhammad Abu al-Awf, 47, director of internal security in the northern Gaza Strip, along with his wife and two teenage daughters.

"His killing deals a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities," the joint statement [IDF and Shin Bet] says.

The army said he had recently been advancing attacks on Israeli troops and civilians, and acted to rebuild the terror group's capabilities, "in systematic violation of the ceasefire" ... killed "to remove the threat he posed."

Context: he was reportedly the likely successor to Naim Abu Nahal, who was killed in a strike the previous day. Abu Nahal became Hamas's internal security chief in September, after his predecessor Muein al-Arabid was captured by Israeli forces in Gaza City.
